prompt.en: An unwanted output is at 14.4 MHz with a 4.8 MHz test carrier. After retuning the carrier to 5.0 MHz, the unwanted output stays at 14.4 MHz. What does this do to the third-harmonic hypothesis?

text.en: It confirms the hypothesis because the first measurement was an exact multiple.

feedback.en: One matching ratio is not enough when the later observation breaks that relationship.

text.en: It confirms the hypothesis because changing the carrier should not move a harmonic.

feedback.en: A harmonic follows an integer multiple of the carrier. The third harmonic would move to 15.0 MHz.

text.en: It weakens the hypothesis; a third harmonic should have moved to 15.0 MHz.

feedback.en: The fixed unwanted frequency no longer follows a three-to-one relationship. Investigate another unwanted-output mechanism.

text.en: It proves that the second harmonic stayed fixed instead.

feedback.en: The new carrier's second harmonic is 10.0 MHz, not 14.4 MHz.

explanation.en: Test a frequency relationship across changed conditions. A single numerical coincidence does not settle the diagnosis.

prompt.en: A bench transmitter passes an unwanted-output check with its metal cover fitted. The cover is then removed for cooling. What should happen before returning it to on-air use?

text.en: Refit the cover and repeat the check in the intended operating configuration.

feedback.en: The cover forms part of the shielding and coupling environment. Validate the configuration that will actually be used, rather than carrying over an earlier result.

text.en: Accept the old result if the RF drive setting is unchanged.

feedback.en: The same drive setting does not preserve the shielding or internal coupling after the cover is removed.

text.en: Accept the uncovered setup if its lower temperature gives a steadier power reading.

feedback.en: A steadier wanted-power reading does not establish acceptable unwanted output. Cooling and emission checks answer different questions.

text.en: Use a good antenna SWR reading to extend the earlier bench result to the uncovered setup.

feedback.en: The antenna match does not measure the effect of a missing shield. It cannot validate the altered transmitter configuration.

explanation.en: A test result applies to the configuration tested. A shielding change needs validation before the transmitter is used on air.

prompt.en: A transmitter output low-pass filter reduces a measured third harmonic, but voice peaks remain flattened and adjacent splatter persists. Which conclusion is justified?

text.en: The residual clipping is evidence to replace the harmonic filter before investigating the transmitter stages.

feedback.en: The harmonic reduction shows that the filter is doing useful work. It does not repair waveform clipping in a separate stage.

text.en: The transmitter is now clean because the harmonic level improved.

feedback.en: One improved emission does not excuse the remaining voice-related splatter and clipping.

text.en: An antenna tuner can remove the remaining modulation distortion without changing transmitter drive.

feedback.en: An impedance match does not restore clipped voice peaks or correct overdrive in the transmitter.

text.en: The harmonic reduction is useful, but the separate overdrive or modulation problem remains.

feedback.en: A clean signal needs both adequate output filtering and operation within the clean drive range.

explanation.en: Different unwanted outputs can need different corrections. Do not treat one successful measurement as a complete repair.
